turns.text: I'm 58 and I get chest discomfort after big meals, and it scares me every time. How do I tell reflux from something to do with my heart?
Why can reflux feel like heart pain? What's going on anatomically?
What features of chest pain point toward the heart rather than the stomach?
If I described this to my doctor, what tests would they likely suggest?
What do cardiologists say about chest pain that comes on with exertion versus after eating?
A friend says smaller meals and not lying down straight after fixed his reflux. Is that the standard advice?
Someone else told me to keep an aspirin in the house just in case. Is that something doctors actually recommend?
I have no insurance and the nearest hospital is ninety minutes away, so I want to be prepared rather than panicked. What should I have in place?
Exactly which symptoms mean I must call for help regardless of the cost?
Can you give me a plan — reflux management, a checklist for telling the two apart, what to keep at home, and when to call?
